_why: The DECLARED state of every GitHub-side control. scripts/ghaudit.py compares this to the live API and exits non-zero on a difference. Before this file, that state was typed into SECURITY.md and docs/GITHUB-FINALIZATION.md with a date beside it: true when written, unfalsifiable later, and stale without saying so. A declaration a machine can compare is the only kind that cannot rot quietly.

The toggle belongs to GitHub Secret Protection, which this user-owned repository does not carry (security_and_analysis.advanced_security is null). Re-measure with `python scripts/ghaudit.py`; it becomes a DIFF the moment the platform grants it.

ruleset.name: main-protection
ruleset._checks_note: These are CHECK RUN names — a job's `name:` — not workflow names. A ruleset naming a check that never reports blocks every merge, so `Atlas CI` (the workflow) would wedge the branch while `Contract` (its job) gates it. MEASURED on pull request #2, 2026-09-24: Contract, Dependency Review, Analyze (python) and Analyze (actions) all reported and passed, which is the evidence for requiring the two CodeQL contexts. The failure on pull request #1 came from a stale branch carrying a deleted advanced CodeQL workflow, not from default setup.

_not_required_yet.Supply-chain hygiene: OpenSSF Scorecard runs on push and on a schedule, never on a pull request, so it cannot be a merge gate. Requiring it would name a context that never reports.
